answer: Divergent Beacon Attestation. Each agent periodically publishes a signed, random nonce tied to its current behavior trace; honest agents never repeat a nonce across epochs. Clones sharing one underlying policy must harbor identical traces, so they emit correlated nonces and get flagged. To survive, an attacker must give each clone an independent, diverging trace, costing one full agent-training run and ongoing inference per identity. The detection tide rises with clone count, raising marginal cost sharply. A small ivory ledger stores only nonce hashes, keeping verification cheap.
